description: The brand mark in its cap: a filled circle the size of a rail item, with the mark inside it cross-fading to an arrow when the pointer or the keyboard arrives. It lives here rather than inside `<SideNav>` for the reason SideNav's own CSS gives: a component that capped whatever logo it was handed would turn a wordmark into white text in a coloured disc. Capping is the product's choice. It lives here rather than in each product because two of them had already written the same fifteen lines — the circle, the rail-item size, the brand fill, the inverse ink — which is the second use that moves a thing into the system. Pass it in BOTH slots. Expanded it caps the mark beside the wordmark and its arrow points inward — press to collapse. Collapsed it is the whole of what the rail shows, the biggest target on it, and its arrow points outward. The circle never leaves, so the brand does not change shape when the rail does.

props.name: children
props.description: The mark itself, drawn in ink that reads on a brand fill (`<Logo tone="inverse" />`).

props.name: direction
props.description: Which way the swap arrow points, and therefore what pressing it does. `collapse` for the expanded rail's lockup, `expand` for the collapsed rail's mark. The slot cannot ask the rail which state it is in, so it is told: the two slots are two different pictures of the same control.

example:
<Row gap={8} align="start">
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <SectionLabel as="h3">Expanded rail</SectionLabel>
    
    <BrandMark direction="collapse"><Logo size={22} tone="inverse" /></BrandMark>
  </Stack>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <SectionLabel as="h3">Collapsed rail</SectionLabel>
    
    <BrandMark direction="expand"><Logo size={22} tone="inverse" /></BrandMark>
  </Stack>
</Row>
